title: Starter SDKenV Cookbook for UX Researchers (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
Short: give UX researchers a lightweight, reproducible SDK environment and a set of micro-labs + prompt probes so they can validate integration UX and error-handling flows without heavy engineering support.

Why this exists
- Researchers ask for reproducible demo apps a lot; engineering time to spin them up is the bottleneck.
- We want consistent telemetry across labs so findings are comparable (latency perceptions, failure pain points, onboarding time).
- Make it low-friction: 15–30 minute setup, 3 short probes, and a teardown.

Audience
- UX researchers, PMs doing quick prototype tests, Solutions engineers doing pre-sales demos.

Goals (measured)
- 90% of researchers can run a micro-lab in <= 30 minutes.
- Capture: time-to-first-successful-call, number of confusing errors encountered, perceived latency (survey).

Quick setup (15–30m)
1) Pre-reqs: Git, Node >=18, a free Redwood sandbox API key (token manager instructions link below).
2) Clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks.git && cd sdks/ux-research-sandbox
3) Install: npm ci (or pip install -r requirements.txt for python).
4) Config: copy .env.sample -> .env, paste SANDBOX_API_KEY, set REGION=us-west1 (default).
5) Start: npm run demo (starts a tiny express server + local UI on :3000).
6) Smoke: click the example prompt, verify streaming output, verify a recorded telemetry event in /telemetry-debug.

Micro-labs (short, focused 10–20m each)
A. Onboarding flow probe (15m)\- Task: evaluate how a new engineer/non-engineer discovers how to make a single completion call.\- Steps: follow README, configure token, call /generate endpoint from UI, verify returned text.\- Observations to capture: step where they stop, language confusion ("model vs. deployment"), unclear error copy.\- Suggested prompts: "Explain in one sentence how to call Redwood API from Node."

B. Latency perception test (10–15m)\- Task: compare perceptions between streaming + chunked UI vs blocking response.\- Steps: run demo in streaming mode (toggle), run in blocking mode, measure wall-clock and ask participant to rate UX.\- Metrics: measured P50/P95, perceived slowness (Likert 1–7).

C. Failure decoding and recovery (15m)\- Task: observe recovery when token limit, network error, and rate limit occur.\- Steps: use injected failure modes (toggle in debug UI): 429 simulator, chunk-drop, truncated streaming.\- Look for: cryptic error messages, unclear retry affordances, missing guidance for next steps.

Suggested probe scripts / micro-interview questions
- "Tell me out loud what you expect to happen when you click `Send`."
- "What would you do if you see this error?" (show error copy)
- "How confident are you that you can get a production-ready demo from these files in a day?"
- Post-task survey (3 questions): clarity, friction, confidence (1–7 scale).

Telemetry + data capture (what to log)
- Event: onboarding_started, onboarding_completed, first_successful_api_call (timestamps).
- Metrics: client-side measured RTT, streaming-chunk arrival timestamps, browser console errors.
- Survey attachments: short free text.
- Storage: telemetry writes to local /telemetry-debug for researchers (no PII), recommend periodic bulk upload to research S3.

Example SDK snippet (Node)
- Copy-paste friendly (placed inline in README):
const Redwood = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.SANDBOX_API_KEY, region: process.env.REGION });
(async () => {
  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood/fast-1', prompt: 'Summarize the following: ...', max_tokens: 120 });
  console.log(res.text);
})();

UI affordances we want to test
- Clear button labels for "Start Stream" vs "Block"
- Visible token/time budget indicator for the demo user
- Inline copy that says: "This sandbox uses synthetic data; do not paste secrets."
- One-click toggle to enable simulated 429 / 500 responses

Field notes / heuristics (researcher tips)
- Watch for hesitation around keys: if participant stops for >30s on .env, count as a friction event.
- Don’t help unless participant explicitly asks; note how they search for help (README, console, slack).
- Record the exact error strings shown; we’ll map to severity categories later.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we include a "non-technical mode" (no .env editing) that uses an ephemeral UI token? Pros: faster for PMs. Cons: hides config surface we want to study. (PR: discuss with security/PM)\- Add Python minimal example? We have Node first; need parity. (owner: Ethan)\- Evaluate whether streaming demo should default to on or off for first-time users. (quick A/B in next sprint)

Links / references
- README prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks/tree/ux-research-sandbox
- Confluence guide on telemetry: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEXP/SDKenV+standards
- Related ticket: ENG-1423 (sandbox telemetry hook)
- Slack thread: #research-sdks (see pinned messages)

Notes to self (Priya)
- Build a tiny Figma flow to walk non-engineer PMs through the demo (low effort).
- Schedule 3 lab sessions (internal) week of 2025-02-10 to validate time assumptions.
- Ask infra to flip on ephemeral sandbox tokens for one week for internal testing.

Appendix: quick checklist (one-line tasks)
- [ ] Clone repo
- [ ] Install deps
- [ ] Add SANDBOX_API_KEY to .env
- [ ] Run demo and verify a successful call
- [ ] Toggle failure modes and observe error copy
- [ ] Run 3 micro-labs with at least 3 participants each
- [ ] Upload telemetry debug bundle to S3 (research bucket)

Fragmentary ideas (brainstorm)
- A tiny CLI that returns a single example curl command to paste into terminal for study participants (reduces .env friction).
- Pre-populated sample prompts tailored to specific verticals (helpdesk, code assistant, product copy).
- Quick annotation overlay in demo UI so researchers can mark moments in-session for later review.

End of draft

(rough — will iterate after the first three lab runs)
